notes: Fiscal year mapping: historical years are the last 3 completed Tyson fiscal years as reported (FY2023 ended September 30, 2023; FY2024 ended September 28, 2024; FY2025 ended September 27, 2025). ([s203.q4cdn.com](https://s203.q4cdn.com/483587180/files/doc_financials/2025/10k/TSN-FY25-10K.pdf))

EBIT definition: EBIT is set to GAAP Operating Income (Loss) from the consolidated statements of income; D&A is Depreciation + Amortization from the consolidated cash flow statement; Capex is absolute value of “Additions to property, plant and equipment” (cash outflow). ([s203.q4cdn.com](https://s203.q4cdn.com/483587180/files/doc_financials/2025/10k/TSN-FY25-10K.pdf))

Net working capital (NWC) construction: NWC = (Current Assets − Cash and cash equivalents) − (Total Current Liabilities − Current debt). This excludes cash and excludes current debt as a funding item; NWC is computed using balance-sheet line items from TYSON FY2024 and FY2025 10-Ks. ([s203.q4cdn.com](https://s203.q4cdn.com/483587180/files/doc_financials/2025/10k/TSN-FY25-10K.pdf))

Tax rate: base-case tax_rate = 0.25 is taken from management’s stated adjusted effective tax rate expectation for fiscal 2026 (used as the normalized long-run assumption). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/100493/000010049326000005/tsn2026q1exh-991.htm))
WACC: wacc=0.09 is a sober modeling assumption not explicitly provided in the cited sources; adjust per your internal capital structure/credit spread framework.

NOLs: nol_balance is set to gross state NOL carryforwards plus gross foreign NOL carryforwards disclosed in FY2025; tax credits are disclosed separately but are not included in nol_balance due to schema limits. ([s203.q4cdn.com](https://s203.q4cdn.com/483587180/files/doc_financials/2025/10k/TSN-FY25-10K.pdf))

Comps: peer multiples are taken from MarketScreener’s sector comparison table (P/E (N), EV / Sales (N), EV / EBITDA (N)); tickers for non-US listings are best-effort and may not match a US ADR symbol.

catalysts: Sustained improvements in operating income as protein spreads and utilization stabilize across segments.
Material changes in free cash flow conversion (driven by working capital and capex execution) that enable further debt reduction and/or capital returns.
Any revisions to FY2026 guidance for sales and capex that shift the base-case trajectory.
company_overview: Tyson Foods is a global protein processor with operations across Beef, Pork, Chicken, and Prepared Foods, plus International/Other. ([s203.q4cdn.com](https://s203.q4cdn.com/483587180/files/doc_financials/2025/10k/TSN-FY25-10K.pdf))

Its operating results can be volatile year to year due to commodity input/output spreads and non-recurring items (e.g., impairments/restructuring). ([s203.q4cdn.com](https://s203.q4cdn.com/483587180/files/doc_financials/2025/10k/TSN-FY25-10K.pdf))

Management allocates capital primarily to maintenance and growth-related capex while managing working capital and leverage. ([s203.q4cdn.com](https://s203.q4cdn.com/483587180/files/doc_financials/2025/10k/TSN-FY25-10K.pdf))
current_context: Q1 2026 sales were $14.313 billion (+5.1% YoY) and GAAP operating income was $302 million (2.1% operating margin). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/100493/000010049326000005/tsn2026q1exh-991.htm))

For fiscal 2026, Tyson expects sales up 2% to 4% vs. fiscal 2025, and expects capital expenditures of $0.7 billion to $1.0 billion. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/100493/000010049326000005/tsn2026q1exh-991.htm))
Tyson also guided that the adjusted effective tax rate should approximate 25% in fiscal 2026. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/100493/000010049326000005/tsn2026q1exh-991.htm))
investment_highlights: Base case revenue growth starts with management’s fiscal 2026 outlook (2%–4%) and transitions to a more conservative low-single-digit long-run growth profile. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/100493/000010049326000005/tsn2026q1exh-991.htm))

Base case EBIT margin expands from FY2025’s GAAP level toward ~3%–3.2% as cycle pressures normalize. ([s203.q4cdn.com](https://s203.q4cdn.com/483587180/files/doc_financials/2025/10k/TSN-FY25-10K.pdf))

Capex intensity is held consistent with guidance ($0.7–$1.0b in fiscal 2026) via a gradual normalization in capex as a % of sales. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/100493/000010049326000005/tsn2026q1exh-991.htm))
Working capital intensity is stabilized around the recent multi-year range using a defined net working capital construction (excludes cash and excludes current debt).
key_risks: Commodity and input cost volatility (live cattle/hogs/chickens, feed ingredients, and energy) that can compress margins quickly.
Operational disruptions (including food safety events) and non-recurring charges (restructuring/impairments) that can distort operating earnings.
Liquidity and leverage sensitivity to interest rates and credit spreads, which can pressure both WACC and equity value.

valuation_summary: The DCF uses GAAP-based operating income as EBIT, depreciation/amortization for non-cash charges, and cash capex from additions to PP&E; terminal value is computed with a Gordon growth approach.
